claims.text: The intended materials are homogeneous, single-phase high-entropy-alloy solid solutions.
The intended alloys have significant configurational disorder.
The integrated model uses composition, atomic-mass contrast, lattice-distortion markers, and vibrational properties as inputs.
Phonon conduction dominates heat transport under the proposed ambient-to-moderately-elevated measurement temperatures.
Atomic-scale disorder and lattice distortion enhance phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Configurational entropy interacts with vibrational damping in a way that affects phonon thermal transport.
Traditional composition-only predictive models do not adequately represent the interplay between configurational entropy and vibrational damping.
Explicitly incorporating phonon-scattering parameters will improve prediction accuracy relative to composition-only methods.
The integrated approach will be 10–20% more accurate at identifying alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Within the model's intended compositional range, measured thermal conductivities will closely match its predictions.
The model is expected to apply where atomic disorder is the dominant phonon-scattering mechanism.
Phase separation, extreme chemical inhomogeneity, or transport anisotropy may limit the model's applicability.
Prediction performance can be benchmarked against conventional approaches using measured phonon thermal conductivity and statistical prediction-error metrics.
The hypothesis is falsified if the integrated approach fails to reduce prediction error by at least 10% relative to conventional models.
